_about: Curated, slow-changing fund facts the price feed does not carry: category, style box, structure, who runs it, strategy, how distributions are taxed. Market data comes from fetch_funds.py. The sync adds an entry for each newly added ticker.

QQQI.name: NEOS Nasdaq-100 High Income ETF
QQQI.mgr: NEOS Investments, a Philadelphia-area options shop founded in 2021 by Garrett Paolella, Troy Cates and Eric Huang, who previously built options and structured products at Nationwide and Horizon Kinetics. The same team runs the whole NEOS High Income lineup.
QQQI.strat: Holds the Nasdaq-100 stocks and sells out-of-the-money Nasdaq-100 index (NDX) call options, often as call spreads that leave some upside open. Premium is paid out monthly. The fund harvests tax losses in the stock book.
QQQI.tax: Index options are Section 1256 contracts (60% long-term, 40% short-term). Much of each distribution has been classified as return of capital, which defers tax by lowering basis.
QQQI.opt: NDX index calls, mostly out of the money, with call spreads at times

GPIX.name: Goldman Sachs S&P 500 Premium Income ETF
GPIX.mgr: Goldman Sachs Asset Management's Quantitative Investment Strategies team, which runs Goldman's premium income ETF lineup (GPIX, GPIQ).
GPIX.strat: Holds S&P 500 stocks and sells S&P 500 index calls on roughly 25% to 75% of the portfolio, adjusting coverage with volatility so the fund keeps more upside than a fully covered strategy. Distributes monthly.
GPIX.tax: Index options are Section 1256 contracts. Distributions have included return of capital in some years.
GPIX.opt: SPX or SPY calls on a partial, flexible share of the portfolio

CEFS.name: Saba Closed-End Funds ETF
CEFS.mgr: Saba Capital Management, the activist hedge fund founded by Boaz Weinstein. Saba's team buys discounted closed-end funds and pushes boards toward tender offers, liquidations or conversions that close the discount.
CEFS.strat: Owns a basket of closed-end funds trading at wide discounts to NAV and earns both their distributions and any discount narrowing. Uses modest borrowing and hedges some interest-rate and equity exposure with short positions. Distributes monthly.
CEFS.tax: Mix of ordinary income, capital gains and return of capital passed through from the underlying funds.
CEFS.lev: Modest borrowing; acquired fund fees from the underlying CEFs add to the expense ratio

PFFA.name: Virtus InfraCap U.S. Preferred Stock ETF
PFFA.sponsor: Virtus ETF Advisers / Infrastructure Capital Advisors
PFFA.bench: ICE BofA Core Plus Fixed Rate Preferred Securities
PFFA.mgr: Infrastructure Capital Advisors (InfraCap), led by Jay Hatfield, a former Lehman Brothers and Gleacher energy banker who also runs PFFR and the InfraCap equity income funds.
PFFA.strat: Active portfolio of U.S. preferred stocks, tilted toward higher-yielding issues from REITs, energy infrastructure and utilities, using moderate leverage (up to about a third of assets) and some option writing to add income. Distributes monthly.
PFFA.tax: Mostly qualified dividends and interest, with some return of capital in some years.
PFFA.lev: Borrowing up to roughly one third of assets

IDVO.name: Amplify CWP International Enhanced Dividend Income ETF
IDVO.mgr: Sub-advised by Capital Wealth Planning (CWP) of Naples, Florida, the covered call shop founded by Kevin Simpson that also runs DIVO and QDVO. Penserra handles trading.
IDVO.strat: Owns roughly 30 to 50 large international dividend payers, mostly through U.S.-listed ADRs, and writes tactical covered calls on individual names, usually short-dated and out of the money. Aims for a mix of income and capital growth. Distributes monthly.
IDVO.tax: Qualified foreign dividends, option premium taxed as short-term gain, and possible return of capital. Foreign tax withheld may be creditable.

NIHI.name: NEOS MSCI EAFE High Income ETF
NIHI.mgr: NEOS Investments (Garrett Paolella, Troy Cates and Eric Huang), the team behind SPYI and QQQI.
NIHI.strat: Gets developed-market international equity exposure through an MSCI EAFE ETF (currently iShares IEFA) and sells call options on the EAFE index to generate monthly income, with tax-loss harvesting on the equity sleeve.
NIHI.tax: NEOS has classified distributions as return of capital so far. Index options are Section 1256 contracts.

ARCC.name: Ares Capital Corporation
ARCC.mgr: Externally managed by Ares Capital Management, part of Ares Management's credit group. Kort Schnabel became CEO in 2025, succeeding Kipp deVeer.
ARCC.strat: Largest publicly traded BDC. Makes senior secured, mostly first-lien floating-rate loans to private U.S. middle-market companies, plus some second-lien, preferred and equity. Pays a quarterly dividend sized to taxable income.
ARCC.tax: Mostly ordinary (nonqualified) dividends. A share can qualify as interest-related or short-term gain dividends for non-U.S. holders; not eligible for the qualified rate.

PBDC.name: Putnam BDC Income ETF
PBDC.mgr: Putnam Investments, now part of Franklin Templeton, with Michael Petro as lead portfolio manager.
PBDC.strat: Active portfolio of publicly traded BDCs, weighted by Putnam's view of credit quality and value rather than size. Gives diversified BDC exposure in one ticker. Distributes monthly.
PBDC.tax: Mostly ordinary income passed through from the BDCs.
PBDC.lev: None at the ETF level; the BDCs it owns borrow. The quoted expense ratio is high because it includes the BDCs' own operating costs (acquired fund fees).

KGLD.name: Kurv Gold Enhanced Income ETF
KGLD.mgr: Kurv Investment Management, founded by Howard Chan (formerly of Credit Suisse and Hong Kong exchange-traded products). Dominique Tersin is a listed portfolio manager across Kurv's funds.
KGLD.strat: Gets gold exposure through gold ETPs and options on them (no physical gold held directly) and runs options strategies such as covered calls and spreads on those positions to generate monthly income while aiming to beat gold's price return.
KGLD.tax: Depends on the gold vehicles held; gold ETP gains can be collectibles-rate income. Distributions may include return of capital.
KGLD.opt: Calls and spreads on gold ETPs

QDVO.name: Amplify CWP Growth & Income ETF
QDVO.mgr: Sub-advised by Capital Wealth Planning (CWP), the Kevin Simpson-founded firm behind DIVO and IDVO. Penserra handles trading.
QDVO.strat: Concentrated portfolio of 20 to 40 large-cap growth stocks screened for earnings growth and cash flow, with tactical covered calls on individual names and sometimes on broad indexes. Aims for capital appreciation first, high income second. Distributes monthly.
QDVO.tax: Option premium is mostly short-term gain; distributions have included return of capital.

FSCO.name: FS Credit Opportunities Corp.
FSCO.mgr: FS Investments (now branded Future Standard); Andrew Beckman is portfolio manager. Formerly a non-traded fund, it listed on the NYSE in November 2022.
FSCO.strat: Opportunistic credit across senior secured loans, high-yield bonds, structured credit and special situations, much of it privately sourced. Uses leverage. Pays a monthly managed distribution.
FSCO.tax: Mostly ordinary income; may include return of capital under the managed distribution plan.
FSCO.lev: Borrowing, roughly 25% to 30% of total assets

ADAMH.name: Adamas Trust 9.875% Senior Notes due 2030
ADAMH.sponsor: Adamas Trust (formerly New York Mortgage Trust)
ADAMH.mgr: Issued by Adamas Trust, the mortgage REIT formerly called New York Mortgage Trust (NYMT), led by CEO Jason Serrano. This is a debt security of the company, not a fund.
ADAMH.strat: $25-par senior unsecured notes paying a fixed 9.875% coupon quarterly, maturing October 1, 2030 (callable earlier). Holder is a creditor of the REIT and ranks ahead of its preferred and common stock.
ADAMH.tax: Interest income, taxed as ordinary income.
ADAMH.lev: Not applicable; credit quality depends on the issuer's balance sheet

NML.name: Neuberger Energy Infrastructure and Income Fund
NML.mgr: Neuberger Berman's energy infrastructure team: Douglas A. Rachlin (senior portfolio manager) and Paolo Frattaroli. The fund dropped "Berman" from its name in December 2025.
NML.strat: Midstream energy infrastructure (pipelines, storage, processing) plus other energy companies including renewables, held as MLPs and C-corps, with leverage. Because of its MLP concentration it is taxed as a C-corporation rather than a RIC, so it accrues deferred tax that reduces NAV. Monthly distribution.
NML.tax: Fund pays corporate tax. Distributions are typically return of capital or qualified dividends depending on the fund's earnings and profits; reported on a 1099.

RLTY.name: Cohen & Steers Real Estate Opportunities and Income Fund
RLTY.bench: Blend of REIT common and preferred indexes
RLTY.mgr: Cohen & Steers' real estate and preferred securities teams: Jason Yablon, Mathew Kirschner and Jerry Dorost on real estate, Elaine Zaharis-Nikas on preferreds, and Yigal Jhirad on options and risk.
RLTY.strat: Combines REIT common stock with preferreds and other real estate income securities, shifting the mix with relative value, and adds leverage. Pays a monthly managed distribution.
RLTY.tax: REIT ordinary dividends (often eligible for the Section 199A 20% deduction), qualified dividends, capital gains and possible return of capital.
RLTY.lev: Borrowing, roughly 25% to 30% of total assets

IYRI.name: NEOS Real Estate High Income ETF
IYRI.mgr: NEOS Investments (Garrett Paolella, Troy Cates and Eric Huang).
IYRI.strat: Holds U.S. REITs and real estate stocks and sells call options on a real estate index or ETF to add monthly income, with tax-loss harvesting in the stock book.
IYRI.tax: NEOS has classified distributions mostly as return of capital. Index options are Section 1256 contracts.
IYRI.opt: Index or ETF calls on real estate

SPYI.name: NEOS S&P 500 High Income ETF
SPYI.mgr: NEOS Investment Management. Managing partners Garrett Paolella and Troy Cates have run the fund since its August 2022 launch; NEOS was founded in 2021 by former Nationwide and Horizon options product builders.
SPYI.strat: Holds the S&P 500 stocks and sells out-of-the-money S&P 500 index (SPX) calls, often as call spreads that leave room for some upside. Distributes monthly and harvests tax losses in the stock book.
SPYI.tax: SPX options are Section 1256 contracts (60% long-term, 40% short-term). Most distributions have been classified as return of capital.
SPYI.opt: SPX index calls, out of the money, with call spreads at times

BTCI.name: NEOS Bitcoin High Income ETF
BTCI.mgr: NEOS Investments (Garrett Paolella, Troy Cates and Eric Huang).
BTCI.strat: Gets bitcoin exposure through spot bitcoin ETPs and options on them, and sells calls on bitcoin ETP indexes to produce a high monthly distribution. Upside is capped in strong rallies.
BTCI.tax: Mix of Section 1256 option gains and return of capital; the bitcoin ETP sleeve is taxed as a grantor trust holding.

UTF.name: Cohen & Steers Infrastructure Fund
UTF.bench: Blend of global infrastructure and preferred indexes
UTF.mgr: Cohen & Steers' global infrastructure team led by Benjamin Morton with Tyler Rosenlicht and Thuy Quynh Dang, and Elaine Zaharis-Nikas running the preferred securities sleeve.
UTF.strat: Global infrastructure stocks (utilities, pipelines, towers, toll roads, airports) plus preferreds and other income securities, with leverage. Pays a monthly managed distribution.
UTF.tax: Mostly qualified dividends and capital gains, with return of capital in some years.
UTF.lev: Borrowing, roughly 25% to 30% of total assets

BXSL.name: Blackstone Secured Lending Fund
BXSL.mgr: Externally managed by Blackstone Credit & Insurance, part of the largest alternative asset manager. Fees are low for the group (1% base on net assets).
BXSL.strat: Senior secured, almost entirely first-lien floating-rate loans to large U.S. private companies, many backed by private equity sponsors. Among the most conservative books in the BDC group. Quarterly dividend plus occasional specials.

ADX.name: Adams Diversified Equity Fund
ADX.mgr: Internally managed by Adams Funds of Baltimore, so shareholders pay no outside advisory fee (expense ratio about 0.49%). James P. Haynie is CEO and lead manager, with portfolio managers Greg Buckley and D. Cotton Swindell.
ADX.strat: Diversified portfolio of large U.S. companies benchmarked to the S&P 500, run with sector weights near the index and stock selection driving relative return. Commits to an annual distribution of at least 8% of NAV, paid quarterly, much of it from realized gains.
ADX.tax: Mostly long-term capital gains and qualified dividends; little or no return of capital historically.
ADX.policy: Income only (8% of NAV annual commitment)

KQQQ.name: Kurv Technology Titans Select ETF
KQQQ.mgr: Kurv Investment Management (founder and CEO Howard Chan); Dominique Tersin has been portfolio manager since launch.
KQQQ.strat: At least 80% in large technology companies, held directly or through Kurv's single-stock income ETFs, overlaid with covered calls, call spreads, risk reversals and protective puts. Can put up to 20% in precious-metals funds. Monthly distributions.
KQQQ.tax: Mostly short-term gains and return of capital.
KQQQ.opt: Covered calls, spreads, risk reversals, protective puts

PCN.name: PIMCO Corporate & Income Strategy Fund
PCN.mgr: PIMCO's multi-sector credit team: Alfred T. Murata, Giang Bui and Mohit Mittal.
PCN.strat: Corporate bonds, high yield, bank loans, mortgage-backed and other securitized credit, using leverage mainly through reverse repos. Monthly distribution.
PCN.lev: Reverse repo and other borrowing, often 20% to 35% of total assets

MAIN.name: Main Street Capital Corporation
MAIN.mgr: Internally managed by its own employees, which keeps costs among the lowest in the BDC group. Dwayne Hyzak is CEO; founder Vince Foster is executive chairman.
MAIN.strat: Debt and equity in lower middle market companies (often taking an equity stake alongside the loan), plus private loans to larger middle-market firms. Pays monthly dividends plus periodic specials.
MAIN.tax: Mostly ordinary dividends, with some capital gains from equity exits.

PTY.name: PIMCO Corporate & Income Opportunity Fund
PTY.mgr: PIMCO's multi-sector credit team: Alfred T. Murata, Giang Bui and Mohit Mittal (same team as PCN).
PTY.strat: Higher-yielding corporate, securitized and emerging market credit with leverage through reverse repos. Larger sister fund to PCN with similar positioning. Monthly distribution.
PTY.lev: Reverse repo and other borrowing, often 20% to 35% of total assets

KSLV.name: Kurv Silver Enhanced Income ETF
KSLV.mgr: Kurv Investment Management (founder and CEO Howard Chan; portfolio manager Dominique Tersin).
KSLV.strat: Silver exposure through silver ETPs and options on them, with options strategies to produce monthly income while aiming to beat silver's price return.
KSLV.tax: Depends on the silver vehicles held; silver ETP gains can be collectibles-rate income. Distributions may include return of capital.
KSLV.opt: Calls and spreads on silver ETPs

DSL.name: DoubleLine Income Solutions Fund
DSL.mgr: DoubleLine Capital: founder and CEO Jeffrey E. Gundlach with Luz M. Padilla (emerging markets) and Robert Cohen (global developed credit).
DSL.strat: Global multi-sector credit with a large emerging market debt sleeve plus high yield, bank loans and securitized credit, using leverage. Monthly distribution.
DSL.tax: Mostly ordinary income; return of capital in some years.
DSL.lev: Borrowing, roughly 20% to 30% of total assets

THQ.name: abrdn Healthcare Opportunities Fund
THQ.mgr: Aberdeen's healthcare team led by Jason C. Akus, who came over with the Tekla funds when abrdn acquired Tekla Capital Management in 2023.
THQ.strat: Healthcare stocks across pharma, biotech, devices and services, with a sleeve of healthcare bonds and convertibles for income, plus leverage. Monthly managed distribution.
THQ.tax: Mostly capital gains and return of capital; little qualified income.
THQ.lev: Borrowing, roughly 15% to 20% of total assets

HTGC.name: Hercules Capital
HTGC.mgr: Internally managed. Scott Bluestein is CEO and CIO; the firm has specialized in venture debt since 2004.
HTGC.strat: Senior secured loans to venture-backed technology and life sciences companies, usually with warrants attached for equity upside. Pays quarterly base dividends plus supplementals.

MLPI.name: NEOS MLP & Energy Infrastructure High Income ETF
MLPI.mgr: NEOS Investments (Garrett Paolella, Troy Cates and Eric Huang).
MLPI.strat: Holds MLPs and energy infrastructure companies (Williams, Enbridge, TC Energy, Kinder Morgan are top holdings) and sells calls for a high monthly distribution. Reports on a 1099, not a K-1.
MLPI.tax: Classified as return of capital so far; 1099 reporting.
MLPI.opt: Calls on energy infrastructure holdings or index

CSWC.name: Capital Southwest Corporation
CSWC.mgr: Internally managed from Dallas; Michael Sarner is CEO.
CSWC.strat: First-lien senior secured loans to lower middle market companies, typically with small equity co-investments. Monthly dividends plus supplementals.

FDUS.name: Fidus Investment Corporation
FDUS.mgr: Externally managed by Fidus Investment Advisors in Evanston, Illinois. Edward Ross is chairman and CEO.
FDUS.strat: Senior secured and subordinated debt to lower middle market companies with equity co-investments. Quarterly base dividend plus supplementals and specials.
FDUS.tax: Mostly ordinary dividends, with capital gains from equity exits.

EMO.name: ClearBridge Energy Midstream Opportunity Fund
EMO.mgr: ClearBridge Investments (Franklin Templeton) energy infrastructure team: Peter Vanderlee and Patrick McElroy.
EMO.strat: Concentrated portfolio of midstream energy companies, MLPs and C-corps, with leverage. Monthly distribution. Taxed as a C-corporation itself, so it reports on a 1099.
EMO.tax: Distributions are often largely return of capital; the fund pays corporate tax and accrues deferred tax on unrealized gains.
EMO.lev: Borrowing, roughly 25% to 30% of total assets

ASGI.name: abrdn Global Infrastructure Income Fund
ASGI.mgr: Aberdeen's global infrastructure and equity income team: Martin Connaghan, Josh Duitz, Donal Reynolds, Ryan Sullivan and Eric Purington.
ASGI.strat: Global listed infrastructure (utilities, transport, communications, energy) plus a small private infrastructure sleeve, with leverage. Monthly managed distribution.
ASGI.tax: Mix of qualified dividends, capital gains and return of capital.
ASGI.lev: Little or none (about 1% effective leverage recently)

PDI.name: PIMCO Dynamic Income Fund
PDI.mgr: PIMCO, led by Group CIO Daniel J. Ivascyn and Alfred T. Murata, with Giang Bui, Russell Gannaway and Bryan Tsu.
PDI.strat: Flexible multi-sector credit with a heavy tilt to non-agency mortgages and other securitized credit, plus corporate and emerging market debt, using reverse repo leverage. Monthly distribution.
PDI.lev: Reverse repo and other borrowing, often 30% to 45% of total assets

GOF.name: Guggenheim Strategic Opportunities Fund
GOF.mgr: Guggenheim Partners Investment Management: Anne Bookwalter Walsh (CIO fixed income), Adam J. Bloch, Steven H. Brown and Evan Serdensky.
GOF.strat: Multi-sector credit (high yield, bank loans, asset-backed securities) plus an equity sleeve overwritten with covered calls. Uses leverage. Monthly distribution, which has been funded partly by rights offerings and at-the-market issuance at a premium to NAV.
GOF.tax: Mix of ordinary income and return of capital.
GOF.opt: Covered calls on an equity sleeve
GOF.lev: Borrowing, roughly 25% to 30% of total assets

MSTY.name: YieldMax MSTR Option Income Strategy ETF
MSTY.mgr: YieldMax ETFs, with Tidal Investments as adviser and ZEGA Financial as the strategy designer.
MSTY.strat: Synthetic exposure to Strategy Inc. (MSTR) built with options, plus Treasury bills, overlaid with sold call spreads that leave some upside participation. Pays weekly. NAV tends to erode when MSTR falls or stays flat.
MSTY.tax: Mostly return of capital and short-term gains.
MSTY.opt: Synthetic long plus short calls on MSTR
MSTY.lev: None, but single-stock risk is very high

AVUV.name: Avantis U.S. Small Cap Value ETF
AVUV.mgr: Avantis Investors is the systematic investing arm of American Century, founded by former Dimensional Fund Advisors executives. Portfolio managers are Eduardo Repetto, Mitchell Firestein, Ted Randall and Daniel Ong (all since 2019), joined by Matthew Dubin in 2024.
AVUV.strat: Actively managed, rules-based portfolio of U.S. small companies that screen as cheap on book value and profitable on cash flow. Holds several hundred names, trades with patience to keep costs low and pays dividends quarterly.
AVUV.tax: Mostly qualified dividends with a small share of nonqualified income; capital gain distributions have been rare.

SCHD.name: Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF
SCHD.mgr: Index fund run by Schwab Asset Management, the asset management arm of Charles Schwab. The portfolio management team has included Ferian Juwono (since launch), Christopher Bliss, Sabya Sinha and Jeremy Brown.
SCHD.strat: Tracks an index of about 100 U.S. stocks with at least 10 years of consecutive dividends, chosen on cash flow to debt, return on equity, dividend yield and five-year dividend growth. Rebalanced annually and pays quarterly.
SCHD.tax: Almost entirely qualified dividends; capital gain distributions have been rare.

SCHY.name: Schwab International Dividend Equity ETF
SCHY.mgr: Index fund run by Schwab Asset Management, the asset management arm of Charles Schwab. Portfolio managers are Christopher Bliss, Chuck Craig, Jane Qin and David Rios, all on the fund since launch.
SCHY.strat: Applies the same screens as SCHD to developed and emerging markets outside the U.S.: about 100 stocks with a 10-year dividend record, ranked on cash flow to debt, return on equity, yield and dividend growth. Pays quarterly.
SCHY.tax: Mostly qualified foreign dividends with some nonqualified income; foreign tax withheld may be creditable.

SPDW.name: SPDR Portfolio Developed World ex-US ETF
SPDW.mgr: Managed by SSGA Funds Management, part of State Street, through its Systematic Equity Beta team rather than named individual portfolio managers.
SPDW.strat: Low-cost index fund holding large, mid and small companies in developed markets outside the U.S., sampled from the S&P Developed Ex-U.S. BMI. Distributes semiannually.
SPDW.tax: Mostly qualified foreign dividends with some nonqualified income; foreign tax withheld may be creditable.

SPYM.name: State Street SPDR Portfolio S&P 500 ETF
SPYM.mgr: Managed by SSGA Funds Management, part of State Street, through its Systematic Equity Beta team rather than named individual portfolio managers. Traded as SPLG until October 31, 2025.
SPYM.strat: Full-replication S&P 500 index fund in State Street's low-cost Portfolio lineup, priced well below SPY. Has tracked the S&P 500 since January 2020 and pays dividends quarterly.
SPYM.tax: Almost entirely qualified dividends; capital gain distributions have been rare.

VSS.name: Vanguard FTSE All-World ex-US Small-Cap ETF
VSS.bench: FTSE Global Small Cap ex US Index
VSS.mgr: Run by Vanguard's Equity Index Group. Portfolio managers are Jeffrey D. Miller (since 2015), Michael Perre (since 2016) and Nicole Brubaker (since 2025).
VSS.strat: Index fund holding several thousand small companies across developed and emerging markets outside the U.S. Pays dividends quarterly.
VSS.tax: Mix of qualified and nonqualified foreign dividends; foreign tax withheld may be creditable.

VWO.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
VWO.bench: FTSE Emerging Markets All Cap China A Inclusion Index
VWO.mgr: Run by Vanguard's Equity Index Group. Portfolio managers are Michael Perre (since 2008), Jeffrey D. Miller (since 2016) and John Kraynak (since 2025).
VWO.strat: Index fund holding large, mid and small companies in emerging markets including China A-shares, with China, India and Taiwan the largest weights. Pays dividends quarterly.
VWO.tax: Mix of qualified and nonqualified foreign dividends, since some countries lack a qualifying U.S. tax treaty; foreign tax withheld may be creditable.

VOO.name: Vanguard S&P 500 ETF
VOO.mgr: Run by Vanguard's Equity Index Group through Vanguard Capital Management. Portfolio managers are Michelle Louie (since 2017), Nick Birkett (since 2023) and Aurélie Denis (since 2025).
VOO.strat: Full-replication S&P 500 index fund and the ETF share class of Vanguard 500 Index Fund, one of the cheapest ways to own the U.S. large cap market. Pays dividends quarterly.
VOO.tax: Almost entirely qualified dividends; Vanguard's share class structure has kept capital gain distributions rare.

VTI.name: Vanguard Morningstar Total Stock Market ETF
VTI.mgr: Run by Vanguard's Equity Index Group through Vanguard Capital Management. Portfolio managers are Walter Nejman (since 2016), Michelle Louie (since 2023) and Nick Birkett (since 2025). Renamed from Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF on July 30, 2026, when its CRSP benchmark was rebranded as a Morningstar index with no change in strategy.
VTI.strat: Index fund holding nearly every U.S. listed stock across large, mid, small and micro caps, weighted by market value, with large caps dominating. Pays dividends quarterly.
VTI.tax: Almost entirely qualified dividends with a small nonqualified share from REITs and other holdings; capital gain distributions have been rare.

VXUS.name: Vanguard Total International Stock ETF
VXUS.bench: FTSE Global All Cap ex US Index
VXUS.mgr: Run by Vanguard's Equity Index Group through Vanguard Capital Management. Portfolio managers are Michael Perre (since 2008), Christine D. Franquin (since 2017) and Jeffrey D. Miller (since 2025).
VXUS.strat: Index fund holding about 8,000 large, mid and small companies in developed and emerging markets outside the U.S., with emerging markets around a quarter of assets. Pays dividends quarterly.
VXUS.tax: Mostly qualified foreign dividends with a meaningful nonqualified share from countries without a qualifying U.S. tax treaty; foreign tax withheld may be creditable.

VGT.name: Vanguard Information Technology ETF
VGT.bench: MSCI US Investable Market Information Technology 25/50 Index
VGT.mgr: Run by Vanguard's Equity Index Group through Vanguard Capital Management. Portfolio managers are Kenny Narzikul and Jena Stenger (both since 2025).
VGT.strat: Index fund holding U.S. information technology stocks of all sizes, with 25/50 capping rules that limit but do not remove heavy weights in the largest names such as Nvidia, Apple and Microsoft. Pays dividends quarterly.
VGT.tax: Almost entirely qualified dividends from a low yield; capital gain distributions have been rare.

QQQ.name: Invesco QQQ Trust, Series 1
QQQ.mgr: Advised by Invesco Capital Management since the fund converted from a unit investment trust to an open-end ETF on December 19, 2025. Portfolio managers are Peter Hubbard, Michael Jeanette and Pratik Doshi (all since December 2025); Tony Seisser left the team effective July 1, 2026.
QQQ.strat: Tracks the Nasdaq-100, the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on Nasdaq, weighted by modified market value and dominated by large technology and communication names. Pays dividends quarterly, with any capital gains annually.
QQQ.tax: Almost entirely qualified dividends from a low yield; capital gain distributions have been rare.

SGOV.name: iShares 0-3 Month Treasury Bond ETF
SGOV.bench: ICE 0-3 Month US Treasury Securities Index
SGOV.mgr: Managed by BlackRock Fund Advisors, the iShares arm of BlackRock. Portfolio managers are James Mauro (since 2020), Jonathan Graves and Marcus Tom (both since 2025).
SGOV.strat: Holds U.S. Treasury bills and other Treasuries maturing in three months or less, giving a cash-like yield with very little interest rate or credit risk. Distributes monthly.
SGOV.tax: Interest is taxed as ordinary income, but because it comes from U.S. Treasuries it is usually exempt from state and local income tax.

SCHB.name: Schwab U.S. Broad Market ETF
SCHB.bench: Dow Jones U.S. Broad Stock Market Index
SCHB.mgr: Index fund run by Schwab Asset Management, the asset management arm of Charles Schwab. Portfolio managers are Ferian Juwono (since 2010), Christopher Bliss (since 2017), Jeremy Brown (since 2018) and Agnes Zau (since 2022).
SCHB.strat: Low-cost index fund holding roughly the 2,500 largest U.S. stocks across large, mid and small caps, covering most of the investable U.S. market. Did a 3-for-1 share split in October 2024 and pays dividends quarterly.
SCHB.tax: Almost entirely qualified dividends; capital gain distributions have been rare.

SCHE.name: Schwab Emerging Markets Equity ETF
SCHE.mgr: Index fund run by Schwab Asset Management, the asset management arm of Charles Schwab. Portfolio managers are Christopher Bliss (since 2017), David Rios (since 2017), Joselle Duncan (since 2023) and Mariela Jobson (since 2024).
SCHE.strat: Index fund holding large and mid-sized companies in emerging markets including China A-shares, with China, Taiwan and India the largest weights. Expense ratio was cut to 0.06% in June 2026 and it distributes semiannually.
SCHE.tax: Mix of qualified and nonqualified foreign dividends, since some countries lack a qualifying U.S. tax treaty; foreign tax withheld may be creditable.

SCHF.name: Schwab International Equity ETF
SCHF.mgr: Index fund run by Schwab Asset Management, the asset management arm of Charles Schwab. Portfolio managers are Christopher Bliss (since 2017), David Rios (since 2017), Joselle Duncan (since 2023) and Mariela Jobson (since 2024).
SCHF.strat: Low-cost index fund holding large and mid-sized companies in developed markets outside the U.S., including Canada and South Korea. Did a 2-for-1 share split in October 2024 and distributes semiannually.
SCHF.tax: Mostly qualified foreign dividends with some nonqualified income; foreign tax withheld may be creditable.

SCHG.name: Schwab U.S. Large-Cap Growth ETF
SCHG.bench: Dow Jones U.S. Large-Cap Growth Total Stock Market Index
SCHG.mgr: Index fund run by Schwab Asset Management, the asset management arm of Charles Schwab. Portfolio managers are Ferian Juwono (since 2010), Christopher Bliss (since 2017), Jeremy Brown (since 2018) and Agnes Zau (since 2022).
SCHG.strat: Low-cost index fund holding the growth half of U.S. large caps, chosen on factors such as projected and historical earnings growth and price ratios, so it is heavy in big technology names. Did a 4-for-1 share split in October 2024 and pays dividends quarterly.
SCHG.tax: Almost entirely qualified dividends on a small yield; capital gain distributions have been rare.

SCHH.name: Schwab U.S. REIT ETF
SCHH.bench: Dow Jones Equity All REIT Capped Index
SCHH.mgr: Index fund run by Schwab Asset Management, the asset management arm of Charles Schwab. Portfolio managers are Ferian Juwono (since 2011), Christopher Bliss (since 2017), Jeremy Brown (since 2019) and Agnes Zau (since 2023).
SCHH.strat: Low-cost index fund holding U.S. equity REITs across property types, including towers, data centers, industrial and residential, with caps on the largest weights. Excludes mortgage REITs and pays dividends quarterly.
SCHH.tax: Mostly nonqualified REIT dividends eligible for the Section 199A deduction, with some return of capital and capital gains.

SCHZ.name: Schwab U.S. Aggregate Bond ETF
SCHZ.mgr: Index fund run by Schwab Asset Management, the asset management arm of Charles Schwab. Portfolio managers are Matthew Hastings, Steven Hung and Alfonso Portillo, Jr., all on the fund since 2011.
SCHZ.strat: Samples the investment-grade U.S. bond market, holding Treasuries, agency mortgage-backed securities and corporate bonds, with an effective duration of about 6 years. Pays monthly.
SCHZ.tax: Almost entirely nonqualified interest income taxed as ordinary income, with part of the Treasury share possibly exempt from state tax.

FDVV.name: Fidelity High Dividend ETF
FDVV.mgr: Advised by Fidelity Management & Research and run day to day by index managers at Geode Capital Management, Fidelity's longtime index sub-adviser. Portfolio managers are Louis Bottari, Peter Matthew and Robert Regan (all since 2016), with Navid Sohrabi and Payal Gupta (since 2019).
FDVV.strat: Tracks a Fidelity index of large and mid-size U.S. companies expected to keep paying and growing high dividends, screened on yield, payout ratio and dividend growth with sector weights tied to the broader market. Pays dividends quarterly.
FDVV.tax: Mostly qualified dividends, with a smaller nonqualified share from REIT holdings; capital gain distributions have been rare.

FTEC.name: Fidelity MSCI Information Technology Index ETF
FTEC.bench: MSCI USA IMI Information Technology 25/50 Index
FTEC.mgr: Advised by Fidelity Management & Research and sub-advised by BlackRock Fund Advisors, whose index team runs the portfolio. Portfolio managers are Jennifer Hsui (since 2013), Peter Sietsema (since 2023), and Matt Waldron and Steven White (both since 2025).
FTEC.strat: Low-cost index fund holding U.S. information technology stocks of all sizes, with 25/50 capping rules that limit how much the largest names such as Nvidia, Apple and Microsoft can weigh. Pays small dividends quarterly.
FTEC.tax: Almost entirely qualified dividends on a low yield; capital gain distributions have been rare.

FXAIX.name: Fidelity 500 Index Fund
FXAIX.mgr: Advised by Fidelity Management & Research and sub-advised by Geode Capital Management, which runs most of Fidelity's index funds. Portfolio managers are Louis Bottari, Peter Matthew, Robert Regan, Payal Gupta and Navid Sohrabi.
FXAIX.strat: Full-replication S&P 500 index fund and one of the cheapest at about 0.015% a year; the fund dates to 1988 and this share class to 2011. No minimum investment, bought and sold at end-of-day NAV, and pays dividends quarterly.
FXAIX.tax: Almost entirely qualified dividends; capital gain distributions have been rare.

FSSNX.name: Fidelity Small Cap Index Fund
FSSNX.mgr: Advised by Fidelity Management & Research and sub-advised by Geode Capital Management. Portfolio managers are Louis Bottari (since 2011), Peter Matthew (since 2012), Robert Regan (since 2016), and Payal Gupta and Navid Sohrabi (since 2019).
FSSNX.strat: Index fund holding the roughly 2,000 small U.S. companies in the Russell 2000, at a cost of about 0.025% a year. No minimum investment, bought and sold at end-of-day NAV, and usually distributes in June and December.
FSSNX.tax: Mostly qualified dividends with a sizable nonqualified share from REITs and other holdings; index reconstitution can produce occasional capital gain distributions.

FVTKX.name: Fidelity Freedom 2060 Fund Class K6
FVTKX.mgr: Actively managed by Fidelity's Global Asset Allocation team, which sets the Freedom glide path and picks the underlying Fidelity funds. Portfolio managers are Andrew Dierdorf and Brett Sumsion, joined by Finola McGuire Foley and Cait Dourney in April 2025.
FVTKX.strat: Target date fund for people retiring around 2060, holding about 40 Fidelity series funds across U.S. stocks, foreign and emerging market stocks and bonds, with a glide path that grows more conservative toward and after 2060. The low-cost K6 class is offered mainly through employer retirement plans, is bought at end-of-day NAV and usually distributes once a year in December.
FVTKX.tax: A mix of qualified and nonqualified dividends passed through from the underlying funds, plus capital gain distributions in many years from active underlying funds and rebalancing.

SWPPX.name: Schwab S&P 500 Index Fund
SWPPX.mgr: Index fund run by Schwab Asset Management, the asset management arm of Charles Schwab. Portfolio managers are Ferian Juwono (since 2013), Christopher Bliss (since 2017), Jeremy Brown (since 2019) and Agnes Zau (since 2023).
SWPPX.strat: Full-replication S&P 500 index fund with a 0.02% expense ratio and no minimum investment, bought and sold at end-of-day NAV. Pays dividends once a year in December.
SWPPX.tax: Almost entirely qualified dividends; capital gain distributions have been rare.
